 Luka Dončić, Quentin Grimes, Matisse Thybulle, Ziaire Williams and Walker Kessler will start Wednesday’s game against the Jazz. 
 Kessler is back to play against his former team after sitting out Tuesday’s overtime win over the Hornets. As a result, Kevon Looney heads to the bench and may fall out of the rotation entirely after playing 17 minutes on Tuesday. The other change is Williams, whose return to the starting lineup means that Jake LaRavia will come off the bench. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Walker Kessler (leg) is off the injury report ahead of Wednesday’s game against the Jazz. 
 Kessler missed Tuesday’s win over the Hornets with leg soreness. He’s set to return Wednesday against the Jazz, his former team. Kevon Looney will head back to the bench with Kessler back in the lineup. 
 Kevon Looney 
 LAL 
 Forward 
 #55 
 Kevon Looney finished Tuesday’s loss to the Hornets with four points (2-of-3 FGs) and seven rebounds. 
 With Walker Kessler (leg) out, the Lakers turned to Looney to start at center on Tuesday. While the veteran center grabbed seven rebounds, he played only 17 minutes, and his mobility was an issue. With Sandro Mamukelashvili (3/3/2/1) shooting 1-of-8 from the field, Lakers head coach JJ Redick eventually turned to two-way contract player Carson Cooper. While his numbers (3/4/2 in 18 minutes) won’t jump off the page, Cooper’s contributions as a rebounder and defender were one reason why the Lakers were able to rally. Kessler is expected to be available for Wednesday’s game against the Jazz, so Looney may find himself out of the rotation once again. 
 Kevon Looney 
 LAL 
 Forward 
 #55 
 Luka Dončić, Quentin Grimes, Matisse Thybulle, Jake LaRavia and Kevon Looney will start Tuesday’s game against the Hornets. 
 Already playing without Austin Reaves, the Lakers won’t have Walker Kessler for Tuesday’s game. Looney moves into the starting lineup, and while he can provide rebounds in that role, Sandro Mamukelashvili is the superior fantasy option despite coming off the bench. 
 Walker Kessler 
 LAL 
 Center 
 #14 
 Walker Kessler (leg) is expected to be available for Wednesday’s game against the Jazz. 
 Kessler is dealing with a sore lower right leg, the reason why he was ruled out of Tuesday’s game against the Hornets. Lakers head coach JJ Redick said he didn’t believe the injury would be long-term, adding that he expects Kessler to play on Wednesday. Sandro Mamukelashvili will have an expanded role with the Lakers’ starting center out, while Kevon Looney could enter the rotation.

 Center 
 #14 
 Walker Kessler (leg) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Hornets. 
 Kessler will miss Tuesday’s game due to a sore lower right leg. This is the first game this season the 7-footer has missed, and his absence has left a massive hole in the Lakers’ rotation. Sandro Mamukelashvili should see his role expand, and Kevon Looney could return to the rotation. 
 Walker Kessler 
 LAL 
 Center 
 #14 
 Walker Kessler recorded 14 points (4-of-5 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), 12 rebounds, three assists, one steal and two blocks in Sunday’s win over the Suns. 
 Kessler has recorded a double-double in five straight games, and he’s blocked at least one shot in four straight games. A bonus for fantasy managers on Sunday was the Lakers’ center going 6-of-6 at the foul line. Kessler began Sunday shooting 61.4 percent from the foul line, so that’s a category fantasy managers will likely have to punt if they’re rostering him. That said, it was good to see him provide unexpected value in that category.

 LAL 
 Guard

 Adou Thiero (ankle) is questionable to play against the Suns on Sunday. 
 Thiero has been a rotation piece for the Lakers since making his season debut last Thursday. His status for this game is up in the air, and he could take on a larger role if he plays since Austin Reaves (heel) is out. Ziaire Williams would play extra minutes if Thiero is out.

 Collin Sexton (eye) is questionable to play against the Suns on Sunday. 
 Sexton should be in line to take on extra minutes with Austin Reaves (heel) sidelined. However, if he’s out, Adou Thiero, who is also questionable, or Ziaire Williams could be in line to fill out the extra minutes. 
 Walker Kessler 
 LAL 
 Center 
 #14 
 Walker Kessler amassed 10 points (5-of-10 FGs), 11 rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block in Wednesday’s win over the Bucks. 
 The Lakers have played seven games in November, and Kessler has recorded a double-double in six of them. In addition to the double-doubles, the 7-footer has blocked at least one shot in 11 of 13 games this season. Thus far, Kessler has been everything that fantasy managers hoped he would be in Los Angeles, and then some.

 LAL 
 Guard

 Luka Dončić, Austin Reaves, Matisse Thybulle, Jake LaRavia and Walker Kessler will start Wednesday’s game against the Bucks. 
 Reaves, who did not play in Monday’s win over the Hawks, returns and will take on his usual role within the Lakers’ lineup. Ziaire Williams heads to the bench, while the other four starters are unchanged.

 Jayson Tatum had 24 points (10-of-23 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers against the Nuggets on Wednesday. 
 Tatum led the Celtics with 24 points Wednesday, but a late technical foul proved costly in the loss to the Nuggets. The 28-year-old forward was assessed a technical foul in the final seconds of the game for throwing the ball in the direction of an official. This allowed Jamal Murray to make the technical free throw and ice the game for the Nuggets by extending the Denver lead to four. The Celtics begin a back-to-back against the Kings and Warriors on the road Saturday. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Jamal Murray had 21 points (7-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, four steals, two blocks and two three-pointers against the Celtics on Wednesday. 
 Murray was excellent and finished with a complete stat line against the Celtics Wednesday. The 29-year-old guard hit a clutch jumper to put the Nuggets up by three with less than 10 seconds left in regulation. Following a technical foul on Jayson Tatum, Murray then hit a free throw to ice the game. Denver improved to 8-5 on the season while the Celtics fell to 11-4.

 Zach LaVine tallied 18 points (8-of-12 FGs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Suns.
 LaVine returned to the Kings’ lineup on Wednesday after an illness kept him out of Sunday’s loss to the Thunder. While he shot the ball well, the veteran guard’s presence was enough to keep the Kings from finishing their home stand with a seventh straight loss. LaVine has been close to a top-50 player so far, outperforming his ADP. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Darius Acuff Jr. finished Wednesday’s loss to the Suns with 36 points (11-of-22 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), four rebounds, six assists, two blocks and six three-pointers.
 Since the 1976-77 season, only one player has scored more points in his first 13 NBA games than Acuff: Michael Jordan. The Kings rookie is in rarefied air, which makes his languishing on a team of this caliber so disappointing. Acuff was efficient as a scorer and playmaker on Wednesday, shooting 50 percent from the field and committing two turnovers. He’s definitely going to get his numbers, but he won’t win many games this season. It’s fair to wonder if there will come a point soon when the front office decides to move on from head coach Doug Christie.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jalen Green accounted for 18 points (6-of-14 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, seven assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Kings.
 After a slow start to the season, Green may be turning things around. He scored an efficient 16 points in Monday’s win over the Nuggets and had another productive outing against the Kings. His value, especially in category leagues, has been poor, but Green’s status as a starter is why he remains rostered in 66 percent of Yahoo leagues. The Suns visit the Jazz on Friday in their final game of the week. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Devin Booker amassed 29 points (10-of-18 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), two rebounds, six assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Kings.
 After scoring 30 points in a November 12 win over the Hornets, Booker shot 9-of-28 from the field in games against the Lakers and Nuggets. He had a much better night against the Kings, shooting high percentages from the field and the foul line while also dishing out six assists. Phoenix, which started 1-5, is now 6-2 over its last eight games, and Booker has provided top-25 fantasy value, as expected. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Dillon Brooks finished Wednesday’s win over the Kings with 29 points (12-of-18 FGs), three rebounds, five assists and five three-pointers.
 In the six games he played before Wednesday, Brooks averaged 9.5 points per game while shooting 33.8 percent from the field. He and his teammates had the good fortune of playing against the Kings, and “The Villain” had his most productive game of the season. While Brooks didn’t record any defensive stats, he finished with a season-high point total and shot 66.7 percent from the field. The Suns play one more game this week, as they’ll visit the Jazz on Friday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson
